clue.text: Adds words to question about Dame's third pantomime

indicators.note: about means the letters go round the next piece

parts.note: to dub a film is to add a new spoken soundtrack to it

indicators.note: third picks out the third letter of the word Dame

parts.note: how? is a question word

explanation.surface: Someone scripts lines and questions a pantomime dame's role in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The pantomime dame is a cross-dressed comic role in British Christmas pantomime; 'about' is the container signal, and 'Adds words' is dubbing a soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb show is a performance in mime only, with gestures and no speech.

clue.text: American supporting flag legend

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, to sag

explanation.surface: An American holding up a flag stands for a national legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic story, the stuff of legend.

clue.text: Hold back regarding line of descent

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
a strain is a breed or lineage

explanation.surface: Someone holds back on the subject of their ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to check or keep under control, a direct synonym.

clue.text: High note coming in very much on an intermittent basis

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
top means highest
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer's top note keeps breaking in, an awkward on-and-off performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' and 'note' are separate pieces, not one musical term; 'coming in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-go describes activity that keeps halting and restarting, as in British economic policy.

clue.text: Crucial English is taken up in bank? More or less

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: vital means crucial

explanation.surface: Is the English side crucial to the bank's operations? Well, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns VITAL + E into ELATIV, which goes 'in' RELY. 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on, not a riverside or a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatively means comparatively or to some degree, a loose synonym for more or less.

clue.text: Lack of power? Indignation after Republican's sent packing

indicators.note: sent packing means dismissed, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: outrage is fierce indignation
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: Fury after a Republican is thrown out suggests a party short of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that power here is electricity, not political clout.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a cut in the electricity supply, a lack of power in the literal sense.

clue.text: Witnessed attorney getting defeated, Bishop getting off

parts.note: Att. is an abbreviation for attorney

indicators.note: getting off means leaving, so this letter is removed

parts.note: bested means beaten or defeated
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A court scene: a lawyer loses, while the bishop on trial is acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, so attested means testified to or witnessed.

clue.text: Mix-up in reassessment of Tory appeal? More or less

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rearranged letters
a reassessment reworks something, so these letters are rearranged
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A muddle in re-evaluating the Conservatives' popularity gives only a rough figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassessment of' rearranges the Tory letters into APPROATELY; 'up' turns the mixing word into XIM, and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately means roughly or about, a dictionary synonym for more or less.

clue.text: Ministerial support not disclosed by a railway

parts.note: something secret is kept undisclosed

explanation.surface: Government backing kept quiet by a rail company.
explanation.definitionFit: A private or parliamentary secretary assists a minister, so the post is ministerial support.

clue.text: Animal to risk swallowing arsenic

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to bet is to risk money
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: An animal willing to gamble on eating poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, especially a large four-legged one.

clue.text: Religious place, ploughed yard supplying special earth

parts.note: pi is informal for pious or religious

indicators.note: ploughed land is turned over, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchyard field, ploughed up, yields a particular kind of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipeclay is a fine white clay used for tobacco pipes and for whitening leather.

clue.text: Rabbit seen around river or smaller waterway

indicators.note: around means the letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: bun is a pet name for a rabbit

explanation.surface: A rabbit spotted near a river or a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a small stream, smaller than a river.

clue.text: Residents ignoring student in one academic institution

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the next

parts.note: unity is the number one, oneness

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: livers are those who live somewhere, residents
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for student

explanation.surface: Locals snub a student at a single college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops L from LIVERS to leave IVERS, which goes 'in' UNITY. LIVERS is the rare sense, people who live in a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A university is a degree-granting place of higher learning.

clue.text: German words of enquiry which aren't neglecting English, sadly

indicators.note: sadly means things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
neglecting means omitting, so this letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A query about which things aren't paying attention to English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglecting' takes E from WHICH AREN'T, and 'sadly' rearranges the remaining WHICHARNT.
explanation.definitionFit: German 'nicht wahr?' is a tag question asking for agreement, like 'isn't it?'.

clue.text: Australian inclined to rhapsodise about tree-trunk making excuses

indicators.note: about means the letters go round the next piece

parts.note: rhapsodising is a lyrical, poetic tendency
a log is a felled tree trunk

explanation.surface: An Aussie gushing over a tree trunk while offering excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apologetic means expressing regret, which often comes with excuses.

clue.text: Containerised awkwardly, without much thought

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Goods packed into containers clumsily, with little care.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means thoughtless, acting without much regard for others.

clue.text: Military activity originated by Irish, involving islands further south

indicators.note: in a down clue further south means placed below the first piece

parts.note: ex means from or out of, as in pedigrees, so originated by

indicators.note: involving means including, so the islands go inside

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language
CI abbreviates the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Manoeuvres started by the Irish, taking in islands further down the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originated by' gives the pedigree word ex (from); 'involving' is the container signal and 'further south' places the rest below, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise is a training manoeuvre by armed forces.

clue.text: Church with new denunciation about Government temperature measurement

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: about means the letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry denunciation

explanation.surface: The Church attacks the Government afresh over the climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Centigrade is the Celsius scale for measuring temperature.

clue.text: Try studio device, introducing note of concise form

indicators.note: introducing means bringing inside, so the letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
a mic is a microphone, standard studio kit

explanation.surface: Test the studio microphone by bringing in a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' is the container signal: the note sits inside the try-plus-device pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic writing is terse and aphoristic, packed into short maxims.

clue.text: Item on string solver cut twice

indicators.note: twice means the shortened word is written two times
cut means trimmed at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the solver is you, the person doing the puzzle

explanation.surface: Something dangling on a string that the solver snipped two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims YOU to YO, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a toy spool that runs up and down a string.

clue.text: Cease getting upset about cut or slice of meat

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
getting upset means being knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Stop fretting over a joint or a piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' rearranges the stopping word into ESCAE, and 'about' wraps it round the cutting word.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat.

clue.text: Shouts euphemism after losing penny

indicators.note: losing means doing without, so this letter goes

parts.note: cripes is a mild oath standing in for Christ

explanation.surface: Someone yells a polite swear word after dropping a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIPES is a dated British exclamation of surprise, a euphemism for Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Cries are calls or shouts, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Lift, with power failing, to move slowly

indicators.note: failing means giving out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: to lift something is to steal it, to pinch it
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A lift whose power cuts out creeps along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like an elevator, which fits the creeping surface; it means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to edge forward by tiny amounts.

clue.text: See 1
A long time when leaving oriental conurbation, heading off

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so these letters come out

parts.note: eastern means oriental
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: a city is a large urban area

explanation.surface: Leaving a sprawling Eastern city and setting out seems to take forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes AS out of EASTERN to give ETERN; 'heading off' drops C from CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, used loosely for a very long while.

clue.text: Religious followers leading soldiers in group

indicators.note: leading means coming first, before the next piece

parts.note: a sect is a body of religious followers
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Members of a cult are at the head of the troops in the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or class, such as a group within society or industry.
